q: 1. The curve showing the relationship between the dry unit weight and the water content of a soil for a given compactive effort, is called
explain: This is precisely the definition of the compaction (moisture-density) curve obtained from a Proctor test.

q: 2. Standard Proctor test is used for determining
explain: The Standard Proctor compaction test establishes the relationship between dry density and moisture content, identifying the optimum moisture content for maximum compaction.

q: 3. Compaction or Soil is aimed at
explain: Compaction packs soil particles more closely together, reducing the void ratio (and expelling air), which in turn increases dry density and shear strength.

q: 4. The most effective method for compacting sands is by
explain: Cohesionless sandy soils compact best under vibratory action (vibrating rollers/plates), which rearranges the granular particles into a denser packing.

q: 5. The ratio of weight of water to the total weight of the soil is known as .............
explain: Water content is properly defined as the ratio of weight of water to the weight of solids, not total soil weight, so none of the given options is technically correct.

q: 6. Out of the following, which will have the maximum value of surface tension force .............
explain: Mercury has an exceptionally high surface tension compared to typical liquids like water, petrol, or acetone.

q: 7. The value of cohesion of a saturated clay will be ............. times the value of unconfined compression strength
explain: For saturated clay under undrained conditions, cohesion c = qu/2, i.e. half the unconfined compressive strength.

q: 8. A fully saturated soil is said to be
options: Two phase system with soil and air
Two phase system with soil and water
explain: When all void spaces are filled entirely with water (no air), the soil reduces to a two-phase system of solids and water only.

q: 9. A soil has a bulk density of 22kN/m3 and water content 10%. The dry density of soil is
10. If the volume of voids is equal to the volume of solids in a soil mass, then the values of porosity and voids ratio respectively are
explain: If Vv = Vs, then void ratio e = Vv/Vs = 1.0, and porosity n = Vv/(Vv+Vs) = 1/2 = 0.5, giving porosity=0.5 and void ratio=1.0.

q: 11. If the, degree of saturation of a partially saturated soil is 60%, then air content of the soil is
explain: Air content = 1 - degree of saturation (as fraction of voids) = 100% - 60% = 40%, since air and water together fill 100% of the void space.

q: 12. Which of the following methods is most accurate for the determination of the water content of soil'
explain: The oven drying method (at 105-110°C to constant weight) remains the standard reference/most accurate laboratory method for water content determination.

q: 13. The relative density of the soil is given by .............
explain: Relative density Dr = (emax - e)/(emax - emin), comparing the natural void ratio to the loosest and densest states.

q: 14. The ratio of volume of voids to total volume of given soil is
explain: Porosity n = Volume of voids / Total volume of soil, by definition.

q: 15. The ratio of total weight of a saturated soil to its total volume is
explain: Saturated density is defined as the total (bulk) weight of a fully saturated soil mass divided by its total volume.

q: 16. Ratio of weight of water to weight of solids in a given soil is
explain: This is the standard definition of water content, w = Ww/Ws.

q: 17. The process of compaction of soil may involve
explain: Field/lab compaction can be achieved through rolling, tamping (ramming), or vibration — the method chosen depends on soil type, but all are recognized compaction techniques.

q: 18. Bitumen, when added to soil, mainly .............
explain: Bitumen primarily coats soil particles and acts as a waterproofing agent, reducing moisture infiltration.

q: 19. The safe bearing capacity of a soil can be defined as .............
options: maximum pressure which the soil can carry safely without shear failure
ultimate load on the bearing area
pressure at which the settlement will not exceed the allowable settlement
explain: Safe bearing capacity is the maximum pressure the soil can safely sustain without risk of shear failure, incorporating a factor of safety.

q: 20. The maximum water content at which a reduction in water content does not cause a decrease in volume of soil mass is known as .............
explain: Per the reference key this is marked as 'ductile limit'; the standard geotechnical term for this behaviour is actually the shrinkage limit.

q: 21. Specific gravity of soil is .............
explain: Per the reference key this is marked 'less than 2.0'; note that most mineral soils actually have specific gravity above 2.5, so this differs from the common textbook fact.

q: 22. Submerged unit weight of soil is equal to the saturated density .............
options: multiplied by unit weight of water
divided by unit weight of water
explain: Per the reference key this is marked 'plus'; the standard relation is actually γ' = γsat - γw (minus), the buoyancy-reduced unit weight.

q: 23. Any change in moisture content of a soil changes .............
options: value of angle of shearing resistance
explain: Moisture content changes affect shear strength parameters, overall soil strength, and compaction requirements simultaneously.

q: 24. The trace moisture absorbed by a dry soil form the atmosphere is called .............
explain: Per the reference key this is marked 'none of the above'; the standard geotechnical term for this trace absorbed moisture is actually hygroscopic moisture.

q: 25. The failure envelope for a clayey soil will be horizontal in the case of .............
explain: In the unconsolidated undrained (UU) test on saturated clay, the failure envelope is horizontal (phi=0 condition).

q: 26. The maximum temperature recommended in the oven dry method for water content determination is .............
explain: Standard oven drying for water content determination uses a maximum temperature of about 110°C to avoid altering clay mineral structure.

q: 27. Water content of a soil can .............
options: take a value only from 0% to 100%
explain: Because water content is defined relative to weight of solids (not total weight), highly organic or soft clays can have water content exceeding 100%.

q: 28. A moist sample of soil weighs 24 g in a tin lid. The tin lid above weighs 14 g. Oven dry weight of tin and sample is 22 g. What is the water content of the soil?
explain: Weight of water = 24-22 = 2 g; weight of dry solids = 22-14 = 8 g; water content = 2/8 = 25%.

q: 29. The ratio of volume of air Va to the volume of voids Vv is called .............
explain: Air content is precisely defined as the ratio of air-void volume to total void volume.

q: 30. Which of the following methods give accurate determination of water content?
explain: Per the reference key, the calcium carbide method is marked as giving accurate results; oven drying is also a standard reference method.

q: 31. The relation between void ratio e, specific gravity G, water content w, and degree of saturation S is given by .............
explain: Per the reference key this relation is given as e = wGS; note the commonly used phase relation is eS = wG.

q: 32. The water content of a saturated soil is 50%. If the specific gravity of the solids is 2.4, what is its void ratio?
explain: For saturated soil, e = wG = 0.5 x 2.4 = 1.2.

q: 33. The hydraulic head that would produce a quick condition in a sand stratum of thickness 1.5 m and of sp. gr. 2.67 and void ratio of 0.67 is equal to .............
explain: Critical gradient ic = (G-1)/(1+e) = 1.67/1.67 = 1.0; head = ic x thickness would give 1.5 m, but per the reference key the marked answer is 3.0 m.

q: 34. The water content at which the soil changes from liquid state to plastic state is known as .............
explain: Per the reference key this is marked 'none of the above'; the standard definition of this exact transition water content is the liquid limit.

q: 35. Berms are used to .............
explain: Berms add mass and width at the toe of an embankment, increasing shear resistance and stability against slope failure.

q: 36. Air content and degree of saturation are related by .............
explain: Since air content and degree of saturation are complementary fractions of total voids, ac + S = 1.

q: 37. Percentage air voids and porosity are related by .............
explain: Percentage air voids equals porosity times air content: na = n x ac.

q: 38. A soil has a bulk density of 2.4 g/cm3 and water content of 20%. What is its dry density?
explain: Dry density = bulk density / (1 + w) = 2.4 / 1.2 = 2.0 g/cm3.

q: 39. The ratio of weight of water to the weight of solids is called .............
explain: Per the reference key this is marked 'porosity'; the standard definition of weight of water to weight of solids is actually water content.

q: 40. Valid range for degree of saturations of a soil in percentage .............
explain: Per the reference key this option is marked; the physically valid range for degree of saturation is actually 0 <= S <= 100%.

q: 41. The maximum water content of a saturated soil at which a reduction in its moisture does not cause a decrease in volume of the soil, is called .............
explain: This is the standard definition of the shrinkage limit, the boundary below which further drying causes no further volume decrease.

q: 42. If the pores of a soil are completely full of air only, the soil is said to be .............
explain: A soil with only air (no water) in its voids is classified as dry soil.

q: 43. The ratio of the volume of voids to the total volume of soil mass is called .............
explain: Porosity is defined as the ratio of void volume to the total volume of the soil mass.

q: 44. The ratio of the unit weight of soil solids to that of water is called .............
explain: Specific gravity of soil solids is defined as the ratio of the unit weight of solids to the unit weight of water.

q: 45. The unit weight of a soil at zero air voids depends upon .............
explain: The zero-air-voids unit weight formula combines unit weight of water, water content, and specific gravity of solids together.

q: 46. Compression of soils occurs rapidly if voids are occupied by .............
explain: Air is highly compressible and escapes voids almost instantly under load, so soils with air-filled voids compress much faster than saturated soils.

q: 47. A clay deposit subjected to pressure in the past which is more than the present overburden pressure is known as .............
explain: When past pressure exceeded the present overburden, the clay is classified as over-consolidated (OCR > 1).

q: 48. A clay deposit which is not fully consolidated under the existing over burden pressure is known as .............
explain: A deposit still consolidating under its current overburden (excess pore pressure not fully dissipated) is termed under-consolidated.
